ch3_s1_evidence: Ada: The plans describe the stylus carrying a trace. The bypass diagram instead shows a physical linkage: counterweight down, gate up. A password is not the documented release.

Ada: Nessa called the shaft a moving-load hazard and locked its access gate. Sera described lowering the counterweight into its cradle from the tower with nobody in the chamber. Inspection comes before considering use.

Ada: The diagram shows counterweight down, gate up. Sera named that the emergency gravity release, opening the bypass to equalize pressure. Nessa and Sera still require inspection; the old drawing does not certify today’s hardware.
ch3_s2_evidence: Ada: Sera described the apparatus as carrying a trace, not a spoken voice. Tomas prepared the dated magnetic reel before we listened; blank chronograph paper is not the source of that historical audio.
Ada: Tomas identified the reel as a physical magnetic recording made in 1998, with manufacture, leader and time announcement that fit. The historical voices we heard came from that recording.
Ada: We documented the handle as part of the cup event. Tomas prepared and dated a magnetic reel for the historical voices; the handle is not that recording.
ch3_s2a_evidence: Ada: We listed photographs, drawings, readings, timestamps and video that can be preserved safely. Sera warned that keeping the apparatus operating adds unquantified risk. Preserving that record and making the installation safe are our revised objectives.

Ada: Sera said operating a hazardous system to prevent skepticism is not an acceptable safety objective. We can preserve what we observed without promising universal agreement or keeping the active effect running.
Ada: We agreed there would be no secret restart. The damaged pressure path is to remain isolated until qualified assessment and authorization; curiosity does not replace that boundary.
ch3_s4_evidence: Ada: Sera said this installation’s interval is fixed. The dial and archive plans give twenty-three hours and seventeen minutes, and nothing we found supports choosing an arbitrary date or sending a warning to 1998.

Ada: The dial and plans give twenty-three hours and seventeen minutes. The checked clocks, mechanical correspondence and matching trace agree with that backward interval. Sera called it self-consistent; the known earlier marks do not establish unrestricted choice.

Ada: Sera described a trace received earlier. The checked clocks pair yesterday’s 18:35 record with today’s 17:52 input, twenty-three hours and seventeen minutes apart. That is the backward interval we compared, not one hour forward.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: In the tower, Sera has exposed the input platen without disturbing the receiving paper. It is a shallow brass board with a freely moving stylus, rather like an old drafting instrument. Its linkage runs into a sealed housing. A second dial, hidden under a service flap, marks an offset in hours and minutes.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: The rubbing wasn't a code. It was a setting copied from this dial: twenty-three hours, seventeen minutes. The archive plans give the same interval at this pressure configuration.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: ada
requiredNewPassages.text: An advance setting.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: Yes. A trace entered now should arrive at the receiving stylus twenty-three hours and seventeen minutes earlier. That is the claim. We need to distinguish reading a dial from establishing what it does.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: On a fresh part of the receiver strip, above your arrival notes, lie three short strokes and a circle with one side flattened. Tomas recorded them forming yesterday at 18:35 while documenting the paper feed, before Ada reached the tower. His short video includes an independently checked clock. He brings it up beside today's live view.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredNewPassages.text: I called these a calibration scribble. Excellent technical term. No assumption smuggled in there.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: We can reproduce them at the input, but that would demonstrate a consistent match, not unrestricted choice. We already know the earlier marks. A genuinely blind repeatable experiment would need a more careful design than we have time for tonight.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: ada
requiredNewPassages.text: So we shouldn't pretend the test proves more than it does.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: Exactly. We can still check the linkage, pressure response, and time relation safely.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: You compare the yesterday calibration video's clock with the present one. The corresponding input time is today at 17:52. There are four minutes until the measured offset closes. Sera verifies that the input mechanism moves freely, then isolates the harmless test section from the bell release. Nessa's lock remains on the shaft gate. Nothing in the test asks anyone to enter the moving-load area.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: ada
requiredNewPassages.text: Why do you look disappointed?

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: Because if this works, the world has become more interesting than my equipment can responsibly measure tonight. That is not entirely a pleasant professional experience.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredNewPassages.text: I can offer a recorder with one unreliable stop button.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: A generous contribution to a revolution in physics.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: At the scheduled second, Sera guides three strokes and a slightly flattened circle across the platen. The input arm moves. A pressure indicator dips and rises. The receiver does not produce a new mark in the present. The earlier photograph already contains the pattern.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: Mechanical correspondence, pressure response, and the configured interval all agree. We have a self-consistent trace separated by twenty-three hours and seventeen minutes. We do not have a license to claim any larger power.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: ada
requiredNewPassages.text: Could we send a warning to 1998?

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: Not with this apparatus. The interval is fixed by this installation. Nothing we've found supports choosing an arbitrary date. Those old recordings are the only route we have to that night.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredNewPassages.text: Which is enough to tell the truth about it. It doesn't have to be enough to save it.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: Ask about the time loop's limits.

conversation.prompt: Ask about the time loop's limits.
suggestions: Can this reach any earlier time we choose?
Does knowing a future trace tell us what we ought to do?
How do we describe this without claiming we've proved everything?
conversation.fallback: This installation supports a fixed twenty-three-hour, seventeen-minute trace interval, with substantial experimental limits. It does not provide moral instructions or a way to select another year.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: Sera asks you to write your name on ordinary paper, then on the disconnected test platen. The second surface changes the drag of the pen. Your usual late cross on the t has no reason to appear in your name, so she asks for a sentence containing one. You choose: The table needs a new cup.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: ada
requiredNewPassages.text: That feels unnecessarily personal.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: You can choose another.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: ada
requiredNewPassages.text: No. Let it be a useful record of my priorities.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: Tomas places the sentence photograph beside the first strip. There it is: the late cross, the compressed round letters, the slight lift before a capital. The platen adds a tiny hook at every hard stop. The same hook appears in the mysterious writing.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredNewPassages.text: Your hand, on this mechanism, makes the same distinctive stops.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: ada
requiredNewPassages.text: Or someone very good at imitating it.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: We keep that possibility. We also stop pretending the direct explanation isn't getting stronger.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: The first message waits beneath the glass. The blue cup is already broken. The handle has already pointed you toward the calibration plate. Somewhere in the next hour is a possible action whose trace may already be lying in front of you. You feel a strange pressure to hurry, then a stronger need to sit down.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: sera
requiredNewPassages.text: We don't have to make a philosophical decision while standing on stairs.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: You sit on the broad landing. Tomas sits two steps below, leaving you room. For once, the tower seems willing to contain people rather than a problem.

requiredNewPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredNewPassages.text: Review the evidence before continuing.
